baseline.notes: T1 baseline, kept for history. JS is main.js from dashboard/src/main.ts (bun build --minify); CSS is dashboard/public/styles.css, tokens.css and fonts/fonts.css, all linked from index.html since T2. The live JS ceiling is js.maxGzipBytes and is explained in the t2 block. The CSS ceiling is the spec's 25 KB.

t2.notes: T2 (#8699) raises the interim JS ceiling by 10,546 B over the T1 baseline (42,553 B). Round 1 (+5,451 B): destination router with legacy redirects and history, APG tablist, Cmd/Ctrl+K command palette, keyboard shortcuts and sheet, native-dialog confirmations, connection states, and the UI primitives in components/ui. Round 2 (+931 B): the fail-closed action gate (role and connection), enforced in api.ts for every mutating request, the two-step emergency brake (intake pause plus pipeline pause, success reported only when both succeed and every running pipeline was signalled, and only on live data), the honest daemon Stop confirmation, offline detection for a page that never connects, the pause-state toggle in the palette, the webhook removal confirmation and the mobile Review action; the no-op Skip stage button was removed. Round 3 (+633 B): per-run results from the server's process-tree signalling (incomplete alerts that name the runs, pause state only from fully signalled runs), the brake working while the feed is stale or offline with an unknown-count dialog, the operator/admin role allowlist, stage labels in the stop dialog, and reasons on disabled controls. Round 4 (+3,531 B): the brake's engaged state (pressed button, a status line in the shell, kept across reloads) and its Release path (a confirmation, then intake and exactly the runs this brake paused are resumed, with the result per run, a run that ended while braked counted as released unless the server could not continue what the brake froze in it, and runs or intake that were already paused left out of the release so it never resumes what someone else paused, while a run the brake partly paused, or anything paused by an attempt whose answer was lost, stays the brake's own, shown as an unconfirmed brake until a retry succeeds; a run whose record no longer verifies leaves the release with a pointer to Runs; one brake or release in flight at a time, recorded as unanswered until it is answered so a closed page cannot lose it, and a release whose answer is lost shown as "may be resumed" until retried, and the brake record kept consistent across tabs: one request in flight across all tabs, held by a Web Locks lock that is atomic across tabs and released when its tab closes, with every tab leaving its waiting state when that request ends or its tab closes, results merged into the current record, and every confirmation bound to the record it showed, so a dialog left open while another tab changed the brake sends nothing, says so and clears an alert whose Retry went stale; with site data blocked the brake's record lasts for the page, so Release stays reachable), the alert banner's brake action labelled Release while engaged, no Release offered while the last attempt went unanswered, and errors worded by cause (no answer from the server, refused by it, or not sent), a partly engaged state whose button retries the brake, and the engaged list kept current when a run is resumed or stopped by hand or intake is resumed from Triage, an incomplete-brake alert that stays until dismissed (each run in plain words, intake status, Retry, the next step, raw details behind a disclosure, and a plain message when the server did not answer), alert actions redrawn when the connection or role changes, Stop reported as incomplete when escaped processes cannot be traced, Stop naming processes an earlier run of the issue left paused that it continued, and a hand Resume of a run that had ended worded as that, never as resumed. Trimming was measured: the optional completion sound costs 184 B and was kept. The byte breakdown is in the T2 PR body. There is no headroom by design. T4 (#8701) deletes the canvas, sprites and retired views; re-measure and lower this ceiling then.
